human_readable: One Country, Two Systems Constitutional Framework
summary: [SPECULATIVE ESTIMATE] KERNEL CONTEST: The Sino-British Joint Declaration and Hong Kong Basic Law (the shared constitutional kernel) read by Beijing as prioritizing 'One Country' (emphasizing absolute sovereign control, national security, and territorial integrity) versus read by Hong Kong civil society as prioritizing 'Two Systems' (guaranteeing democratic autonomy, civil liberties, and an independent judiciary). The text remains fixed, but the competing readings emit opposing structural constraints regarding state coercion[cite: 2, 3].

human_readable: Cultural Heritage and Restitution Legal Frameworks
summary: [SPECULATIVE ESTIMATE] KERNEL CONTEST: International customary law and treaties regarding historical artifacts (the codified legal kernel) read by holding institutions and former empires as a mandate for 'universal encyclopedic heritage' and preservation (a public scaffold), versus read by post-colonial successor states as a mandate for the repatriation of expropriated sovereign property. The contest dictates who holds the legitimate epistemic and physical authority to adjudicate historical extraction[cite: 2].

[SPECULATIVE ESTIMATE] KERNEL CONTEST: A state occupational licensing statute (the formal legal kernel) read explicitly by professional boards as a necessary public safety and quality-assurance standard (a coordination Rope) versus read by marginalized workers and market entrants as an artificial, rent-seeking barrier designed to suppress labor competition (an extractive Snare). The exact same statutory text generates entirely different beneficiary and victim structures depending on the reading[cite: 2, 3].
